scope_allowed: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

models.name: M1: Linear Construct with Bonded Hardware
models.what_it_computes: Static implicit FE of plate–screw–bone construct with linear elastic bone, rigid plate approximation, bonded screw–plate and screw–bone; predicts stress/strain fields, screw-tip distance to cortical boundary, and plate–bone gap as functions of screw angulation.

models.name: M2: Deformable Plate with Frictional Interfaces
models.what_it_computes: Static implicit FE with deformable plate and locking head, frictional contact at screw–plate and screw–bone, orthotropic cortical shell and trabecular core; computes interface force resultants, local strain energy density, screw-tip proximity, and gap opening versus angulation.

models.name: M3: Thread-Embedded Nonlinear Bone Response
models.what_it_computes: Static implicit FE with helical thread representation via equivalent cohesive zone, elasto-plastic damage in trabecular region, plate–bone contact; returns screw axial/pullout surrogates, local bone plastic strain, plate lift-off, and breach likelihood with angulation.

mechanisms.name: Cortical breach at screw tip
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Excessive angulation can drive the distal tip toward or through the far cortex, risking soft-tissue injury and compromised fixation.

mechanisms.name: Plate–bone lift-off and loss of reduction
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Off-axis screws can lever the plate, increasing construct micromotion and gap opening across the fracture, which may impair healing.

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are reported on an integral 0–4 ordinal scale with descriptive anchors.

expected_decision.outcome_source: On balance, and consistent with the scale and matrices reported, the outcome of this assessment is Not accepted.
rationale_keywords: M1 is structurally incapable of representing lift-off

requirements: The solver residual tolerance was set to 1e-6 in normalized form, with an energy norm assessment at the end of each step; if the energy imbalance exceeded 0.5%, the step was repeated with smaller increments and tightened contact stabilization.

Refining cortical shell and plate elements from 0.6 mm to 0.3 mm at the distal cluster changed the minimum far-cortex tip clearance by 0.08 mm (2.6%) and the peak plate von Mises stress by 3.1%; halving again to 0.15 mm changed both quantities by no more than 1.1% across all angulations tested.

Instead, we set a target local element size of 0.3 mm in the distal region by requiring that a halving of the size cause no more than a 3% change in peak distal plate stress and no more than a 0.1 mm change in tip clearance at 20 degrees in M2; this target was then used consistently in all runs supporting the credibility matrices.
